analysis: Both units are historical release-note text in CHANGELOG.md (head lines ~2980-3474, v0.9.9 down to v0.9.0). The patch excerpt shows the real change as a new v0.10.6 candidate section added near the top of the file (head 11-808), but the units I was given are unchanged older entries. No code, configuration, auth, crypto or protocol behavior is changed in the supplied lines. The lines I examined describe App Attest recovery, SSD prefix-cache behavior, and graceful draining. They are consistent with existing threat-model entries: T-041 (TTL, HMAC lookup tags, account-scoped cache salt), T-053/T-054 (stale authorization fencing, build qualification) and TB-011. No documented control in these lines contradicts or weakens the threat model. One unreviewed point: the new v0.10.6 section (two-Mac clusters, RDMA over Thunderbolt, a `cluster_runtime` block in registration, coordinator-derived pair approvals) falls outside the supplied units and is only partly visible in the truncated patch excerpt. It could add new trust boundaries, including a Thunderbolt peer link, cluster key and plaintext handling between Macs, and local-API key use on a leading Mac. The current threat model has no cluster boundary for these. A reviewer of the corresponding source and the rest of the CHANGELOG diff should check whether the threat model needs updating. I make no finding from the supplied text.
